podcast-dannyjones-NejsITNlxg4:
Congresswoman Anna Paulina Luna has led congressional efforts on UFO disclosure. She joins Danny Jones to discuss the killing of Charlie Kirk and her faith in God. She also discusses the Book of Enoch and the CIA. The range, from a political assassination to ancient scripture, is presented as one connected field of hidden conflict.

Luna speaks as both legislator and believer, moving between oversight hearings and the apocryphal texts she reads seriously. Jones draws out her account of what the government hides and why. Her claims about Kirk's killer and the agencies are her own and remain contested. The episode documents a sitting member of Congress reasoning in a register, part investigator, part end-times reader, that would have been unthinkable on the record a generation ago. That shift itself is the story the recording preserves.
podcast-joerogan-IaT0WOwEag4:
Joe Rogan turns to the open questions around gain of function research in a segment from his show. Such work makes germs stronger or more prone to spread, in the name of foresight. The Covid years made the term a household one.

Rogan works through the case for and against the work, as labs and critics state them. He asks who funds it, who checks it, and what a leak would mean. The segment is short and hot. Listeners get a brisk map of a grave debate. The library holds the file as an archive record of the questions as raised.
podcast-joerogan-knWCsonQVG4:
Paleontologist Trevor Valle joins Joe Rogan to answer claims that dinosaurs never lived. Valle works with fossils and public science shows. A viral video by Eric Dubay sets up the debate.

Valle plays the denial video and replies point by point. He faults one-way videos that face no questions while they record. He explains how bones, rock layers, and finds across the world fit together. The episode is part science lesson and part media lesson, showing why live pushback matters when bold claims spread fast online. Valle stays patient, even when the claims grow wild.
podcast-tuckercarlson-q72s8zwwGg4:
Tucker Carlson opens with a warning about war numbers before turning to Vice President JD Vance and Iran. He says casualty counts in wartime are almost always false. Governments on all sides hide the true cost.

The episode title frames Vance warning Israel against a wider war. Carlson reads official figures for the Russia and Iran wars with doubt. He argues Iran grows stronger while its rivals tire. The talk presents the push for restraint as a last move by America-first voices. Listeners hear a case for doubt, limits, and an end to open-ended war.
